newsitem.title: USA: Montana's soil moisture levels decline.
newsitem.headline: Montana's soil moisture levels decline.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the Montana Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ending Sunday, August 3.
CROPS: AREAS OF THE STATE CONTINUE TO RECEIVE PRECIPITATION WITH EARLY EVENING THUNDERSHOWERS WHILE OTHER COUNTIES ARE DRY AND HOT. THERE WERE 6.8 DAYS SUITABLE FOR FIELD WORK.

SOIL MOISTURE LEVELS HAVE DETERIORATED IN THE PAST COUPLE OF WEEKS CAUSING A SLIGHT REDUCTION IN CROP CONDITIONS. TOPSOIL MOISTURE IS RATED 9 PERCENT VERY SHORT, 52 PERCENT SHORT, 39 PERCENT ADEQUATE, AND 0 PERCENT SURPLUS. SUBSOIL MOISTURE WAS RATED AT 6 PERCENT VERY SHORT, 42 PERCENT SHORT, 51 PERCENT ADEQUATE, AND 1 PERCENT SURPLUS.

WINTER WHEAT IS NOW 74 PERCENT RIPE AND HARVEST IS IN FULL SWING WITH 39 PERCENT COMPLETED. FARMERS ARE EXPERIENCING PROBLEMS WITH WHEAT STEM SAW FLY AS WELL AS GRASSHOPPERS IN PARTS OF THE STATE. HARVEST OF SPRING GRAINS HAS JUST BEGUN. NEARLY 85 PERCENT OF THE SPRING WHEAT HAS TURNED COLOR, 6 PERCENT IS RIPE AND 1 PERCENT IS HARVESTED. BARLEY HAS TURNED COLOR ON 70 PERCENT OF THE ACREAGE, 10 PERCENT IS RIPE, AND 1 PERCENT IS HARVESTED. OATS HAS 76 PERCENT OF THE ACREAGE TURNING COLOR, 13 PERCENT IS RIPE, AND 1 PERCENT IS HARVESTED.

LOCALIZED RAIN SHOWERS HAVE HAMPERED THE HAY HARVEST IN SOME AREAS. THE FIRST CUTTING OF ALFALFA IS 97 PERCENT COMPLETE, AHEAD OF THE FIVE-YEAR AVERAGE OF 91 PERCENT. THE SECOND CUTTING OF ALFALFA IS 13 PERCENT COMPLETE WHICH IS BEHIND THE FIVE-YEAR AVERAGE OF 18 PERCENT. OTHER HAY HARVEST IS 9 POINTS AHEAD OF NORMAL WITH 82 PERCENT OF THE ACREAGE HARVESTED.
VERY POOR POOR FAIR GOOD CELLENT
LIVESTOCK: CATTLE AND CALVES CONTINUE TO BE IN GOOD CONDITION. A PROBLEM
WITH WOLVES KILLING SHEEP WAS REPORTED IN NORTHWESTERN MONTANA. PASTURE AND RANGE FEED CONDITION HAS DETERIORATED SOMEWHAT FROM THE PREVIOUS WEEK DUE TO HOT, DRY CONDITIONS IN SOME AREAS.

MONTANA WEATHER FOR WEEK ENDING AUGUST 2, 1997: A LARGE, UPPER-LEVEL RIDGE OF HIGH PRESSURE OVER THE CENTRAL U.S. BROUGHT MONSOONAL MOISTURE NORTHWARD INTO MONTANA FROM OLD MEXICO AND ARIZONA, RESULTING IN SCATTERED MAINLY AFTERNOON AND EVENING THUNDERSTORMS. CHESTER RECEIVED 1.7 INCHES OF RAIN DURING THE WEEK. A FEW STATIONS DID NOT RECEIVE ANY RAIN. TEMPERATURES WERE A LITTLE ABOVE NORMAL. HARLEM GOT UP TO 100 DEGREES, WHILE WISDOM HAD A LOW OF 34.

THE OUTLOOK FOR AUGUST 7-11 CALLS FOR: TEMPERATURES TO BE ABOVE NORMAL WITH NEAR NORMAL PRECIPITATION EAST OF THE CONTINENTAL DIVIDE AND TEMPERATURES AND PRECIPITATION TO BE NEAR NORMAL WEST OF THE DIVIDE. NORMAL TEMPERATURES FOR THIS PERIOD IN MONTANA ARE HIGHS IN THE 80S, EXCEPT IN THE SOUTHEAST WHERE NORMAL HIGHS ARE IN THE LOWER 90S AND IN THE 70S IN THE HIGHER WESTERN VALLEYS.
NORMAL LOWS ARE IN THE 50S, EXCEPT IN THE SOUTHEAST WHERE NORMAL LOWS ARE IN THE LOWER 60S AND IN THE 40S IN THE WESTERN VALLEYS.
